toyota_summary:
The Trump administration moved to reinstate tariffs on imports under Section 301, with base rates of 10 to 12.5 percent, after the previous version expired. The timing and scope remain unclear, but the threat is immediate and affects supply chains across multiple countries.

For automakers, this matters because nearly every vehicle sold in the U.S. relies on parts sourced globally. A 10 percent tariff on imports would raise production costs across the industry unless manufacturers move sourcing to the U.S. or Mexico, a shift that takes years and billions in capital. Europe and Japan would be hit first; both are negotiating exemptions or retaliation measures.

Watch whether the administration grants carve-outs for specific countries or sectors, or if the tariffs take effect as written.

emails.subject: EG US Daily: Separating signal from noise in Trump’s latest tariff
emails.excerpt: トランプ政権の新たなSection 301に基づく10-12.5%の基本関税は、期限切れのSection
emails.subject_en: EG US Daily: Separating signal from noise in Trump’s latest tariff rollout
emails.summary_en: The Trump administration has replaced its expired Section 122 tariffs with a new 10-12.5% baseline tariff under Section 301, marking the durable foundation of US trade policy going forward. Separately, the threatened 50% tariff on Canada under the untested Section 338 authority is a negotiating tactic aimed at pressuring Ottawa in stalled USMCA talks rather than a firm policy shift. Automakers and suppliers should treat the Section 301 baseline as the stable planning assumption, while discounting headline-grabbing threats as leverage tactics likely to recur across other trading partners.
emails.summary_ja: トランプ政権は失効したセクション122関税に代わり、セクション301に基づく10~12.5%の新たな基準関税を導入し、これが今後の米通商政策の安定的な土台となる。一方、カナダに対する未検証のセクション338権限を用いた50%関税の脅しは、停滞するUSMCA交渉でカナダ側に圧力をかけるための交渉戦術に過ぎない。自動車メーカーやサプライヤーは、セクション301による基準関税を安定した前提として計画を立てつつ、他の貿易相手国にも波及しうる注目度の高い関税の脅しは交渉上のノイズとして割り引いて捉えるべきである。

emails.subject_en: France, Germany seek grand bargain on cars and ‘Made in Europe’
emails.summary_en: France and Germany are negotiating a grand bargain linking tougher 'Made in Europe' rules for EU procurement and subsidies with relief for automakers, including a softened 2035 combustion-engine ban. The push comes as Volkswagen warns of 100,000 job cuts, adding urgency to revive Europe's auto industry. Officials aim to finalize the deal by autumn, ahead of EU ministerial talks in September and a leaders' summit in October.
emails.summary_ja: フランスとドイツは、EUの調達・補助金における「メイド・イン・ヨーロッパ」規定強化と、2035年内燃機関車禁止の緩和を組み合わせた包括的合意の交渉を進めている。フォルクスワーゲンが世界で10万人の人員削減を警告する中、欧州自動車産業の再建が急務となっている。両政府は9月のEU産業相会合や10月の首脳会議に先立ち、秋までの合意成立を目指している。

emails.subject_en: EG Research Summary in Japanese: 2026年7月23日
emails.summary_en: Escalating Middle East tensions—spanning the Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea shipping threats, and Ukraine's strikes on Russia—are set to push oil toward $90 a barrel, which will also squeeze already-tight global grain and fertilizer supplies and raise agricultural prices. Meanwhile, trade friction is intensifying elsewhere: Washington has imposed new 50% tariffs on some Canadian goods and revived Section 338 to pressure USMCA talks, India is delaying its E25 ethanol mandate by at least a year, and Gulf states are rerouting trade away from Hormuz-dependent corridors.
emails.summary_ja: ホルムズ海峡や紅海での緊張激化、ウクライナによるロシア攻撃を背景に原油価格は1バレル90ドル台へ上昇する見通しで、在庫が乏しい世界の穀物・肥料市場にも打撃を与え、農産物価格の上昇が見込まれる。一方、米国はカナダの一部製品に50％関税を課しUSMCA交渉打開のため通商法338条を復活させ、インドはE25エタノール混合義務化を少なくとも1年延期し、湾岸諸国はホルムズ依存を減らすため貿易路の再構築を進めている。
